synopsis: ASAM is a Germany-based nonprofit industry association whose OpenX family supplies many of the scene-description formats discussed; despite its road-vehicle roots, the booklet rates OSI and FMI as domain-neutral and transferable to off-road work [f13222, f13197, f13224]. OpenMATERIAL 3D 1.0.0 was released on 3 April 2025 to standardize material properties for lidar, radar and camera simulation; version 1.1.0 was planned for October 2026, while volumetric properties remained under development [f3917, f8614, f3923, f3922]. Across chapters, ASAM reports no standardized simulation-quality metrics, particularly for sensors; QSQ was still at proposal stage in September 2025, and both QSQ and the separate sensor-fidelity project remained under way in 2026 [f8327, f5218, f4835]. High-fidelity OSI work addresses inadequate representations of phenomena such as camera spectral irradiance and radar raw waveforms and runs through March 2027, creating interface-versioning risk around the program’s planned first-tool-chain integration [f7081, f8618, f8619, f15870]. Although OpenX was described as in maintenance mode in 2026, an off-road concept project was active in October 2026; missing terrain, vegetation, manipulation and sensor-degradation concepts mean extensions or a manufacturer domain model are needed, and the booklet considers an off-road extension unlikely before mid-2027 [f7170, f7171, f7195, f7434, f13212]. TestSpecification was still developing infrastructure rather than a mature universal solution in October 2026, and ASAM standards were not verified in this research [f7119, f7702].
